main_body: Round stone well: a light grey stone rim ring around a dark water opening, with a block-shaded stone front face below. A wooden frame with a crossbeam, two posts and a bucket stands above it.
top_band: Light grey-white rim at rows 14-17 (back rim), then a dark blue water ellipse at rows ~17-20, then a light front rim at rows ~20-22
evidence: In the middle column the back rim (light grey, rows 14-16) leads into a dark water ellipse with a highlight (rows 17-20). Below it a lighter front rim edge (rows ~20-22) separates the opening from the front face. A darker row under the rim precedes the stone-block front face (rows 23-31). The inside of the opening is clearly visible from above, as in the well reference. The stone blocks are shaded rather than inset, but the main body reads as a correct 3/4 container.

style.evidence: The stone has about 5 steps, from pale rim through mid greys to a deep base, and the blocks are shaded individually. The outlines are tinted blue-grey and brown, not black. The wooden parts are thin and flat: the beam has about 3 tones, the posts are about 2px wide with one edge shade, and the bucket is tiny. The water is mostly one dark blue with a single highlight. There are no tile or grain textures like the roofed-well reference's roof, so tile colour counts are lower than the reference's. Overall it is slightly thinner than the reference, and with doubt this is a fail.
